impact:
Discovered while fixing T-009's real-client capture, and it is a property of the CLIENT rather than of our code, so it will reach users of the v0.2 MCP server (T-013).

Measured on codex-cli 0.144.0. When `codex exec` runs without the operator's `~/.codex/config.toml` (via --ignore-user-config), a tool call to a `-c`-declared MCP server is CANCELLED BY THE CLIENT before the request is ever sent:

  client -> server : initialize, notifications/initialized, tools/list        (and nothing more)
  server -> client : correct initialize result, correct tools/list result
  client stderr    : mcp: spendbar-probe/spendbar_probe started
                     mcp: spendbar-probe/spendbar_probe (failed)
                     user cancelled MCP tool call
  client stdout    : "The MCP tool call was canceled and did not succeed."

The server is blameless — it answered both requests correctly and never received tools/call.

The governing setting is per-server: `mcp_servers.<name>.default_tools_approval_mode`, whose accepted values are `auto`, `prompt`, `writes`, `approve`. The default (`auto`) cancels in a non-interactive `codex exec` run with no prior approval on record. `approve` fixes it.

What did NOT fix it, each measured rather than assumed: a `projects."<cwd>".trust_level="trusted"` override for the run's scratch cwd; dropping `--ephemeral`. What DID also work and was rejected: `--dangerously-bypass-approvals-and-sandbox`, which disables the sandbox for everything the model might run in order to solve one server's tool approval.

WHY THIS MATTERS BEYOND THE SPIKE. A user who adds spendbar's MCP server to Codex and drives it non-interactively can see their tool calls cancelled with an error that names spendbar and looks like our server failed ("(failed)"), when nothing on our side went wrong. T-013 should decide what to do about it: at minimum document the required approval setting in the Codex setup instructions, and consider whether the registration snippet we tell users to paste should include `default_tools_approval_mode`.

Also worth recording as evidence hygiene: the previous Codex captures in this repo passed only because the operator's own config.toml had entries that approved the call. That is precisely the contamination ISS-047 was filed about, now demonstrated rather than suspected — isolating the config is what made the requirement visible at all.
resolution:
Resolved by documenting the requirement durably at docs/codex-mcp-approval.md, for the consumers that need it: T-013's MCP setup instructions and the v0.3 setup wizard.

WHAT WAS ALREADY DONE, verified rather than assumed. The harness-side half of this issue was already fixed when T-009 landed: spikes/mcp/real-client/capture.mjs:518 passes -c 'mcp_servers.spendbar-probe.default_tools_approval_mode="approve"', capture.test.mjs:344 asserts that argument is present, and both evidence manifests record it in the verbatim command line. The reasoning is written out at capture.mjs:489-506, including that each rejected alternative was measured. So the spike is correct and covered.

WHAT WAS MISSING, and is what this issue actually asked for. The knowledge lived only in a comment inside spikes/, which that directory's own framing calls evidence rather than shipping code, and which no user-facing surface reads. The issue asked for the Codex SETUP INSTRUCTIONS to carry it and for the registration snippet users paste to be considered. T-013 owns those instructions and is currently parked, and src/mcp does not exist, so there was no user-facing document to edit. Writing one is the fix rather than a placeholder for it: the requirement is needed by whoever unparks T-013, and a spike comment is not where they will look.

THE DOCUMENT records: the measured exchange (client sends initialize and tools/list, server answers both correctly, client then reports "user cancelled MCP tool call" and never sends tools/call); the per-server setting default_tools_approval_mode with its accepted values auto|prompt|writes|approve and the default auto being what cancels; the TOML block and the -c override form; and the three measured alternatives - a projects trust_level override for the run cwd did not help, dropping --ephemeral did not help, and --dangerously-bypass-approvals-and-sandbox works but is rejected because it disables the sandbox for everything the model might run in order to approve one server's tools.

THREE PIECES OF GUIDANCE FOR T-013, which is the part that changes what gets built:
1. The setting belongs INSIDE the registration snippet users paste, not in prose beside it. The failure is silent, the error text says "(failed)" next to the server name, and it therefore reads as a spendbar bug. A user who skips the prose reaches a wrong conclusion about our software; the snippet is the artefact that actually gets copied.
2. T-013's AC 9 exit test drives Codex non-interactively and must set it explicitly, and must ASSERT that tools/call was received - otherwise a cancelled run scores as a spendbar conformance failure and the test is measuring the harness. This was independently confirmed by the T-013 plan review, which cited ISS-055 as compounding AC 2.
3. Prefer absolute paths in command, since shebang bins break under GUI-launched clients that do not inherit the package manager's PATH. A separate hazard, noted together because both surface at the same moment - a user pasting a registration snippet - and both produce errors naming spendbar.

EVIDENCE-HYGIENE NOTE PRESERVED. Earlier Codex captures passed only because the operator's own ~/.codex/config.toml approved the call; isolating the config is what made the requirement visible. That is ISS-047's suspected contamination, now demonstrated. The general lesson is recorded because it outlives this setting: a real-client test that inherits the operator's configuration is measuring the operator, and taking the configuration away is how you find out.

No code changed - this is a client behaviour, and the code that had to account for it already does.
title: Codex cancels an MCP tool call unless the server is approved in config — affects how spendbar's MCP server is documented for Codex users
